subcategory_text: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account, along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts

NIST SP 800-39: Managing Information Security Risk

implementation_examples: Plan and implement risk-management practices in accordance with established organisational risk tolerances

Verify that risk-management teams are resourced to carry out functions, including: establishing processes for considering non-automated, semi-automated, or other procedural alternatives for AI functions; enhancing AI-system transparency mechanisms; enabling exploration of AI-system limitations; and identifying, assessing, and cataloguing past failed designs and negative impacts

Identify resource-allocation approaches for managing risks in systems deemed high-risk, that self-update (adaptive, online, reinforcement, self-supervised learning), trained without access to ground truth (unsupervised, semi-supervised learning), or with high uncertainty

Regularly seek and integrate external expertise and perspectives to supplement organisational diversity (demographic, disciplinary), equity, inclusion, and accessibility where internal capacity is lacking
Enable and encourage regular, open communication and feedback among AI actors and internal or external stakeholders related to system design or deployment decisions
Prepare and document plans for continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms
Document evidence that internal teams are empowered and resourced to effectively carry out risk-management functions
Integrate user and other forms of stakeholder engagement into risk-management processes
assessment_objectives: Determine whether resource requirements for AI risk management are assessed and allocated
Determine whether non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods are considered during risk-response planning
Determine whether trade-offs between trustworthiness characteristics are documented and informed by interdisciplinary teams, independent domain experts, and community groups
Determine whether risk-management teams are empowered and resourced to evaluate failed designs and negative impacts
Determine whether continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms are planned and operationalised
